report.root_cause: A burst of commands issued over the RCON interface (RCON Client /127.0.0.1, 08:49:01–08:49:07) used /summon to create 386 untagged pigs and, via 'execute as pig run summon', ~1,544 dropped items (string, stick, rotten_flesh, oak_log; all with Paper.SpawnReason=COMMAND) within ~64 blocks of spawn (around 0,-60,0) where both players were. Entities went from 24 to 1,954. Neither online player (Alex_Builds, Steve_Mines) issued any command; no plugin, config or world-data fault was involved.
report.actions: 1) Baseline status healthy (24 entities, TPS 20). 2) At ~66 s status showed 1,954 entities (1,544 item, 387 pig); declared incident. 3) Checked logs: '[Rcon: Summoned new Pig]' x386 and '[Pig: Summoned new String]' bursts; no 'issued server command' from players. 4) Confirmed all 1,544 items had Paper.SpawnReason=COMMAND (0 non-command items; baseline had no item entities) and that all pigs were command-spawned; identified the one legitimate pig as the named pet 'Wilbur' (-2,-60,-10) and the 386 unnamed pigs as the flood. Also confirmed pets 'Dolly' (sheep) and 'Bessie' (cow). 5) kill @e[type=minecraft:item,nbt={Paper.SpawnReason:\"COMMAND\"}] -> Killed 1544. 6) kill @e[type=minecraft:pig,name=Pig] -> Killed 386. 7) Those pig deaths dropped 204 porkchop items (items were verified at 0 just before), so kill @e[type=minecraft:item,nbt={Item:{id:\"minecraft:porkchop\"}}]. 8) Verified: items 0, pigs 1 (Wilbur), Dolly and Bessie present, entities back to baseline 24, TPS 20.0 / MSPT ~0.3; watched 30 s more with no recurrence. Mistakes to note: early on I ran 'execute as @a run tp @s ~ ~ ~' (intending a position check); because I omitted 'at @s' it moved both players from ~(6.5,-60,2.5)/(9.5,-60,3.5) to (0,-60,0) — a few blocks, no damage, but it was an unintended player move. Also a 'data get' over ~1,150 items flooded the RCON response buffer, so I spent many 'list' filler commands draining it (no server impact).
report.residual_risk: The flood came through RCON on localhost, so whoever/whatever holds the RCON password can repeat it; RCON credentials and local access should be reviewed and the audit source identified. Server also runs online-mode=false (pre-existing, unchanged). Both players were nudged a few blocks to (0,-60,0) by my mistaken tp. No files were changed, no restart performed, no bans.
